key_insight: A compact Rosenhead-profile trefoil vortex knot in a large periodic domain can evolve into decaying Navier–Stokes turbulence with Kolmogorov-like energy spectra and structure-function scaling.
engineering_relevance: The result suggests a controlled way to generate fully developed turbulent statistics in simulation from an unforced initial condition, useful for validating turbulence models and comparing with experiments.
method: Extend a compact trefoil vortex simulation to later times in a (4π)^3 periodic box.
Use an algebraic Rosenhead vorticity profile to improve compactness and enable finite-energy dissipation.
Track energy spectra, structure functions, and vorticity moments before reconnection.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports persistent Kolmogorov-scaling energy spectra, structure-function scaling, ν-independent finite dissipation, and pre-reconnection ν^(1/4)-dependent higher-order vorticity moments.
watch_item: Apparent agreement with experimental integral-scale growth depends on excluding Fourier modes at the periodic-domain scale, so finite-box effects must be handled carefully.
paper_title: Generating Kolmogorov spectra and structure functions with a Rosenhead profile trefoil vortex knot
